A key now needs silicon nobody can clone. At join the client hands over its TPM endorsement certificate, signed by the chip vendor, and seals its signing key inside that module; the registry hashes the EK and refuses a second seat from the same one, so a software TPM fails the vendor chain even when it mimics the protocol exactly.

Chips cost 9 dollars each and wiring a host takes 40 minutes, so fifty seats run 500 dollars before one whisper of income, plus a fresh nonce signed per seat per epoch to keep the raven counted.

A willow cutting roots only where its own bark meets soil.
